title: Multiplayer Lens Flare with Light Source Tracking
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements a multiplayer lens flare post-processing system with dynamic light source tracking. Requirements:

## Scene Setup
- Create a dark space scene with a black background and subtle star field (200+ small white points randomly distributed in a sphere of radius 500).
- Add a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 30) looking at origin.
- Create 3 movable point lights (light sources) that generate lens flares:
  - Light A: Red (#ff3030), position (-10, 5, 0), intensity 2.0
  - Light B: Green (#30ff30), position (10, 5, 0), intensity 2.0
  - Light C: Blue (#3030ff), position (0, 10, -5), intensity 2.0
- Each light should have a visible sphere mesh (radius 0.5) at its position with emissive material matching its color.
- Add a ground plane (50x50, dark gray #222222) at y=0 for spatial reference.

## Lens Flare System
- Implement a custom lens flare effect for each light using screen-space calculations (NOT the deprecated Three.js Lensflare addon - implement manually with sprites or screen-space quads).
- Each lens flare should consist of 4 flare elements along the line from the light's screen position through the screen center:
  - Primary glow (at light position, size proportional to intensity)
  - Secondary ring (at 0.4 along the line to center, 60% opacity)
  - Tertiary hexagon (at 0.7 along the line, 40% opacity)
  - Ghost reflection (at 1.3 past center, 20% opacity, inverted position)
- Flare visibility must be based on whether the light is in front of the camera (dot product check with camera forward vector).
- Flare intensity should attenuate based on distance from screen center (brighter near edges).
- When a light is occluded (behind the ground plane, y < 0), its flare should fade to 0.

## Player System (Multiplayer Simulation)
- Simulate 2 players, each controlling a light:
  - Player 1 controls Light A (WASD keys for XZ movement)
  - Player 2 controls Light B (Arrow keys for XZ movement)
  - Light C is autonomous, orbiting the origin at radius 8, speed 0.5 rad/s
- Movement speed: 5 units/second, lights are clamped to x:[-20,20], z:[-20,20], y stays fixed at 5.
- Add a DOM panel (top-left) showing each player's light screen coordinates and flare visibility status.

## Interactions
- Press '1' to toggle Light A on/off (affects flare visibility and intensity)
- Press '2' to toggle Light B on/off
- Press '3' to toggle Light C on/off
- Press 'F' to cycle flare quality: Low (2 elements), Medium (3 elements), High (4 elements)
- Mouse wheel: zoom camera in/out (FOV 30-90 degrees), which affects flare sizes
- Press 'R' to reset all lights to initial positions and states
- Click on the canvas to add a temporary flash flare at click position (fades over 1 second)

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- lights: array of 3 objects each with {position: {x,y,z}, color: string, intensity: number, enabled: boolean, screenPosition: {x,y}, isVisible: boolean, flareOpacity: number}
- flareQuality: 'low'|'medium'|'high' (current quality level)
- flareElementCount: number (2, 3, or 4 based on quality)
- camera: {fov: number, position: {x,y,z}}
- activeFlares: number (count of currently visible flares)
- orbitAngle: number (Light C's current orbit angle in radians)
- flashFlares: array of {x, y, opacity, timeRemaining}
- totalFlareElements: number (sum of all visible flare elements across all lights)
- frameCount: number (increments each frame)
- deltaTime: number (last frame delta in seconds)

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Light positions clamped to [-20,20] on X and Z axes. Y fixed at 5 for player lights. Orbit radius exactly 8 for Light C. Flare opacity must be 0 when light is disabled or behind camera. FOV clamped to [30, 90]. Flash flares decay linearly over 1 second. Screen positions normalized to [-1, 1] range.
